correctness.rationale: For all finite trees n>=4, the complement-NOR map is the common closed-star center operator. Symmetric antitone closure proves F^3=F, and pairwise closed-star intersections enumerate all possible image classes. Explicit disjoint inverse-fiber counts yield each fixed and two-cycle basin, including isolated-center stars. Strict convexity of 2^(e+2)-2e-4 under sum(e)=n-2 proves unique star, path, broom extremizers. Both supplied executable checkers independently corroborate all tested finite cases but the written arbitrary-order proof is the criterion.

evidence: Aracena–Richard–Salinas arxiv:1507.06141 Proposition 1 identifies fixed points of loopless symmetric negative conjunctive networks with maximal independent sets.

value.rationale: Natural all-order complement-of-tree family; full individual attraction-basin census, unique largest orbit, exact fixation chance, and sharp star/path/broom extremizers. This differentiates dynamical attraction robustness among graph structures not determined by general short-period or fixed-state theorems. Structural optimization and all-fiber classification are substantive beyond a renaming or finite isolated value.
